components.note: 瓦 (tile, pottery) — marks pottery and fired clay, as in 瓷 china; 瓶 is a bottle.
并 (bìng) hints at the sound: 瓶 píng is close to 拼 pīn and 屏 píng.

example.hanzi: 我买了一瓶水。
example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yì píng shuǐ.
example.english: I bought a bottle of water.
example.fact: 瓶 is both a bottle and the measure word for bottled things: 一瓶水, 一瓶啤酒. 瓶子 is a bottle, 花瓶 a vase, and 瓶颈 ("bottle neck") means a bottleneck, as in English.

examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang yǒu yì píng niúnǎi.
examples.english: There is a bottle of milk on the table.

examples.hanzi: 这个花瓶是我奶奶送的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège huāpíng shì wǒ nǎinai sòng de.
examples.english: This vase was a gift from my grandmother.

components.note: 虫 (insect, creature) — small animals and insects, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蛇 snake, 虾 shrimp: 蛋 is the egg of a creature.
米 (rice) — grain and food, as in 粉 powder, 糟, 精: cakes were first made from rice flour.
羔 (gāo, lamb) gives the exact sound.

example.hanzi: 生日快乐!我们一起吃蛋糕吧。
example.pinyin: Shēngrì kuàilè! Wǒmen yìqǐ chī dàngāo ba.
example.english: Happy birthday! Let's eat cake together.
example.fact: 蛋糕 is a partly borrowed word: 糕 already meant a steamed rice- or flour-based cake in Chinese long before Western-style cakes arrived, while 蛋 (“egg”) was added specifically to mark the egg-rich, Western-style version — a compound that layers a foreign food concept onto a pre-existing native word rather than inventing or transliterating a wholly new term.

examples.hanzi: 我想吃一块巧克力蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chī yí kuài qiǎokèlì dàngāo.
examples.english: I'd like to eat a piece of chocolate cake.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈给我做了一个生日蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Māma gěi wǒ zuòle yí ge shēngrì dàngāo.
examples.english: Mom made me a birthday cake.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 呼, 吃, 喝; 吸 is to breathe in.
及 (jí) is a loose sound hint for xī; same part in 级 jí and 极 jí.

example.hanzi: 请深深地吸一口气。
example.pinyin: Qǐng shēnshēn de xī yì kǒu qì.
example.english: Please take a deep breath.
example.fact: 吸 is to take in: 吸烟 (smoke), 吸引 (attract), 吸收 (absorb), 吸尘器 (vacuum cleaner). 呼吸 (breathe) pairs 呼 (exhale) and 吸 (inhale).

examples.pinyin: Tā xī le yì kǒu xīnxiān kōngqì.
examples.english: He took a breath of fresh air.

examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài hǎimián néng xī hěn duō shuǐ.
examples.english: This sponge can absorb a lot of water.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — heads and faces: 头, 额 forehead, 题 title, 领 collar; 顺 is a head following the river 川 along.
川 (chuān) is only a loose sound hint; 训 xùn and 顺 shùn share it.
禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.

example.hanzi: 祝你面试顺利!
example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ miànshì shùnlì!
example.english: Wishing you a smooth interview!
example.fact: 顺利 combines 顺 (“to follow along, go with the flow,” as in 顺着河走, “walk along the river”) with 利 (“advantageous, favorable”) — together picturing events flowing smoothly along a favorable current, and it's a fixture of Chinese well-wishing formulas (一路顺利, “safe travels”) in place of a direct “good luck.”

examples.pinyin: Gōngzuò hěn shùnlì.
examples.english: Work is going smoothly.

examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ yílù shùnlì!
examples.english: Wishing you a smooth journey!

components.note: 歹 (bad bone) — death and decay, as in 残 remnant, 烈 fierce, 殊 special.
匕 (person) — a person beside bones: death.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 警方还没有公布死者的身份。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng hái méiyǒu gōngbù sǐzhě de shēnfèn.
example.english: The police have not yet released the identity of the deceased.
example.fact: 死者 is built transparently from 死 ("to die") plus 者, a nominalizing suffix meaning "the one who/that," the same suffix behind 读者 ("reader") and 作者 ("author") — but its formal, news-register tone means everyday speech more often just names the person directly rather than reaching for this somewhat clinical term.

examples.hanzi: 我们为死者默哀一分钟。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen wèi sǐzhě mò'āi yì fēnzhōng.
examples.english: We observe a minute of silence for the deceased.

examples.hanzi: 医生确认了死者的死因。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng quèrènle sǐzhě de sǐyīn.
examples.english: The doctor confirmed the cause of death of the deceased.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 傻 is a foolish person.
瓜 (melon) — a melon hanging from a vine. It lends its sound to 孤 gū and 狐 hú, besides 傻瓜 and 南瓜.

example.hanzi: 你怎么会相信这种谎话?真是个傻瓜。
example.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme huì xiāngxìn zhè zhǒng huǎnghuà? Zhēn shi ge shǎguā.
example.english: How could you believe such a lie? What a fool.
example.fact: 瓜 (melon) shows up in more than one Mandarin word for foolishness — 傻瓜 ("foolish melon") sits alongside Sichuanese slang like 瓜娃子 ("silly kid") — a folk association between a round, hollow melon and an empty head that spans both standard Mandarin and regional dialect.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié dāng shǎguā le.
examples.english: Stop being a fool.

examples.hanzi: 他笑着说：“我真是个傻瓜！”
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàozhe shuō: “Wǒ zhēn shì ge shǎguā!”
examples.english: He said with a smile, "I'm such a fool!"

meanings: mile (unit of length equal to 1.609 km)

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — plants and flowers: 花, 草, 茶; 英 first meant a flower, then outstanding, then hero.
央 (yāng) is a loose sound hint (-ng); also in 映 yìng and 殃 yāng.
田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 从这里到机场大约十五英里。
example.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ dào jīchǎng dàyuē shíwǔ yīnglǐ.
example.english: It's about fifteen miles from here to the airport.
example.fact: 英里 literally means "English li" — 英 is the character used to transliterate "England/English" (as in 英国, 英语), attached to 里 (a traditional Chinese distance unit) to name the foreign, imperial-system mile. Mainland China's everyday distance unit is instead the metric 公里 ("common/metric li," kilometer), so 英里 mostly turns up when discussing English-speaking countries.

examples.hanzi: 这辆车一小时能跑六十英里。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē yì xiǎoshí néng pǎo liùshí yīnglǐ.
examples.english: This car can go sixty miles an hour.

examples.pinyin: Tā měi tiān pǎo sān yīnglǐ.
examples.english: He runs three miles every day.

components.note: 女 (woman) — marks women and family terms, as in 妈 mom, 姐 sister, 好 good; 嫁 is a woman marrying out of her family.
家 (jiā) — close sound: 嫁 jià. 家 also means home, which suits a bride going to her new home.

example.hanzi: 她嫁给了一个医生。
example.pinyin: Tā jià gěi le yí gè yīshēng.
example.english: She married a doctor.
example.fact: 嫁 is used for a woman marrying (嫁给), and 娶 (qǔ) for a man marrying. 嫁人 is the plain "get married" for women, and 嫁祸于人 means to shift the blame onto someone else.

examples.pinyin: Tā de jiějie jià dào le wàiguó.
examples.english: His older sister married and moved abroad.

examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng zhème zǎo jiù jià rén.
examples.english: She doesn't want to get married so early.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 挑 is to pick out by hand.
兆 (zhào) is a loose sound clue; same part in 跳 tiào, 桃 táo and 逃 táo.
戈 (halberd, weapon) — war and weapons: 我, 成, 武, 伐; here fighting.
占 (zhàn) sounds exactly like 战; also in 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 这个项目对我们团队是一个很大的挑战。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù duì wǒmen tuánduì shì yí gè hěn dà de tiǎozhàn.
example.english: This project is a huge challenge for our team.
example.fact: 挑战 does double duty as both a verb ("to challenge someone," 挑战权威 "challenge authority") and a noun ("a challenge," as here) without changing form — a common pattern in Chinese verb-object compounds, where English usually needs two different words (challenge vs. challenging) to cover the same ground.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan jiēshòu xīn de tiǎozhàn.
examples.english: I like taking on new challenges.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng guànjūn fāqǐle tiǎozhàn.
examples.english: He challenged the champion.

components.note: 歹 (bad bone) — death and decay, as in 残 remnant, 烈 fierce, 殊 special.
匕 (person) — a person beside bones: death.
土 (earth) — the top part, the ground family as in 地, 场, 块. Memory aid: leave the ground 土 and go off on your own 厶 path.
厶 (private, small loop) — the bottom part. Old forms show a person leaving a place, so the 土 story is only a mnemonic.

example.hanzi: 他的祖父几年前已经死去了。
example.pinyin: Tā de zǔfù jǐ nián qián yǐjīng sǐqù le.
example.english: His grandfather died several years ago.
example.fact: 去 here works as a directional verb complement rather than "to go" — attached after 死, it marks the action as a complete departure from life, the same abstract "away, off" sense 去 contributes in 失去 ("to lose," lit. "lose away") and 除去 ("to remove").

examples.pinyin: Nà kē lǎo shù yǐjīng sǐqù le.
examples.english: That old tree has already died.

examples.hanzi: 他死去的消息传来，大家都很难过。
examples.pinyin: Tā sǐqù de xiāoxi chuánlái, dàjiā dōu hěn nánguò.
examples.english: News of his death came and everyone was very sad.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
土 (earth) — the top part, the ground family as in 地, 场, 块. Memory aid: leave the ground 土 and go off on your own 厶 path.
厶 (private, small loop) — the bottom part. Old forms show a person leaving a place, so the 土 story is only a mnemonic.

example.hanzi: 电梯坏了,我们只能走上去。
example.pinyin: Diàntī huài le, wǒmen zhǐ néng zǒu shàngqù.
example.english: The elevator is broken, so we can only walk up.
example.fact: 上去 and its mirror image 上来 both mean "to go/come up," but the choice of 去 versus 来 encodes the speaker's own viewpoint — 上去 moves away from the speaker's position, 上来 moves toward it, a directional distinction with no separate word in English.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shàngqù kànkan, tā zài bu zài.
examples.english: Go up and see whether he's there.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìqǐ shàngqù ba.
examples.english: Let's go up together.

components.note: 七 (qī) — seven; as a part it sounds out 切 qiē (cut, with 刀 knife) and 柒 qī.

example.hanzi: 我每天七点起床。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān qī diǎn qǐchuáng.
example.english: I get up at seven every day.
example.fact: 七 appears in 七夕 (the seventh day of the seventh lunar month, a Chinese Valentine's Day) and the idiom 七上八下 ("seven up eight down"), describing an anxious, unsettled heart.

examples.hanzi: 我们一周上七天班，太累了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yì zhōu shàng qī tiān bān, tài lèi le.
examples.english: We work seven days a week, which is too tiring.

examples.hanzi: 星期六晚上七点，我们在餐厅见。
examples.pinyin: Xīngqīliù wǎnshang qī diǎn, wǒmen zài cāntīng jiàn.
examples.english: See you at the restaurant at seven on Saturday evening.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing and listening: 听, 闻, 聋; 职 is the duty one hears and remembers.
只 (zhī) is a near sound match for zhí; also in 织 zhī and 识 shí.
Memory aid: 业 looks like a row of upright posts on a base, like a shop sign or an old tool stand; 'business/trade' is the extended meaning. Origin is unclear, so no firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 你的职业是什么?
example.pinyin: Nǐ de zhíyè shì shénme?
example.english: What is your profession?
example.fact: 职业 leans formal and written — the word you'd fill in on a form or see printed on an ID card — while everyday spoken Mandarin more often just asks 你是做什么工作的? ("What kind of work do you do?"), a case where a concept's dictionary word isn't quite the most natural thing to say out loud.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng huàn yí ge xīn de zhíyè.
examples.english: I'd like to change to a new occupation.

examples.hanzi: 医生是一个受人尊敬的职业。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shì yí ge shòu rén zūnjìng de zhíyè.
examples.english: Doctor is a respected profession.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plants; 菜 is vegetables, as in 草 grass, 花 flower.
采 (cǎi) is the same syllable with a different tone; it also sounds out 彩 cǎi and 踩 cǎi.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的菜很好吃。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài hěn hǎochī.
example.english: The food at this restaurant is delicious.
example.fact: 菜 means both "vegetables" and "a dish": 点菜 (order dishes), 菜单 (menu), 中国菜 (Chinese food). In slang 菜 means unskilled: 我太菜了 ("I'm so bad at this"), especially in gaming.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ ài chī qīngcài.
examples.english: I love eating green vegetables.

examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn wǒ lái zuò jǐ gè cài.
examples.english: Tonight I'll cook a few dishes.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand holding a stick, as in 教 teach, 收 collect, 放 release: correcting by hand.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for gǎi.

example.hanzi: 我想改一下计划。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gǎi yíxià jìhuà.
example.english: I want to change the plan a bit.
example.fact: 改 is to change something into something better or different: 改正 (correct), 改革 (reform), 改变 (change). 改天 ("another day") is a polite way of postponing, as in 改天再聊.

examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng wǒ gǎi le sān cì.
examples.english: I revised this article three times.

examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī bāng wǒ gǎi zuòyè.
examples.english: The teacher helps me correct my homework.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 块; 址 is a place on the ground.
止 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 址.

example.hanzi: 请把你的地址写在这张纸上。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ nǐ de dìzhǐ xiě zài zhè zhāng zhǐ shàng.
example.english: Please write your address on this piece of paper.
example.fact: 地址 has extended naturally into the digital world as 网址 ("web address," lit. "net-address") and IP 地址 ("IP address") — the same 址 root, originally just "the location of a place" (built from 土 earth + 止 a footprint/stopping-place), now covers both physical mail and internet locations.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiā de dìzhǐ shì shénme?
examples.english: What is your home address?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ dìzhǐ fā gěi nǐ le.
examples.english: I sent you the address.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 你有什么意见？
example.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme yìjiàn?
example.english: What's your opinion?
example.fact: 意 is the heart-level idea behind words. It appears in 意思 (meaning), 注意 (pay attention), 同意 (agree), 愿意 (be willing), 生意 (business). 不好意思 means "sorry" or "embarrassed", and 有意思 means interesting.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tóngyì nǐ de yìjiàn.
examples.english: I agree with your opinion.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì gùyì zhèyàng zuò de.
examples.english: He did it on purpose.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and trade, as in 财 wealth, 货 goods, 贵 expensive; 赚 is to earn.
兼 (jiān) is only a loose sound hint for zhuàn.

example.hanzi: 他一个月赚多少钱？
example.pinyin: Tā yí gè yuè zhuàn duōshao qián?
example.english: How much does he earn a month?
example.fact: 赚 stresses profit and gain, as in 赚钱 (make money), and its counterpart is 赔 (péi, to lose money): 赚了还是赔了? 挣钱 (zhèngqián) is another common way to say earn, closer to earning through effort.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōngsī zhuàn le bù shǎo qián.
examples.english: He earned quite a lot of money at the company.

examples.hanzi: 做生意不一定每次都赚。
examples.pinyin: Zuò shēngyi bù yídìng měi cì dōu zhuàn.
examples.english: You don't necessarily profit from every deal.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
小 (small) — a 小 with a stroke taken off: not much. 少 also gives sound to 沙 shā, 抄 chāo and 炒 chǎo.

example.hanzi: 这次比赛来了不少观众。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì bǐsài lái le bùshǎo guānzhòng.
example.english: Quite a few spectators came to this match.
example.fact: 不少 is a double negative that reads as a plain positive — literally "not few," it lands as "quite a lot," similar to how English "not a little" can imply a fair amount — except in Chinese 不少 is the completely neutral, everyday way to say this, not a marked or literary construction.

examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu bùshǎo péngyou.
examples.english: He has quite a few friends.

examples.pinyin: Jīnnián xiàle bùshǎo yǔ.
examples.english: It has rained quite a lot this year.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
犭 (animal, dog) — animals, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狂 wild: dogs guard.
讠 (speech) — words and law; 狱 first meant a lawsuit, then a prison.

example.hanzi: 那部电影把战场描述得像地狱一样。
example.pinyin: Nà bù diànyǐng bǎ zhànchǎng miáoshù de xiàng dìyù yíyàng.
example.english: That movie described the battlefield as being like hell.
example.fact: 地狱 ("earth-prison") entered Chinese primarily as a Buddhist translation term for the underworld realm of punishment (Naraka) — distinct from 阴间, the older native folk term for the land of the dead, a reminder that Buddhism's arrival in China left its mark even on ordinary vocabulary for the afterlife.

examples.hanzi: 他说那段日子像地狱一样。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō nà duàn rìzi xiàng dìyù yíyàng.
examples.english: He said those days were like hell.

examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén shuō huàirén huì xià dìyù.
examples.english: Some people say bad people go to hell.

components.note: 于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 天开始下雨了,于是我们决定回家。
example.pinyin: Tiān kāishǐ xiàyǔ le, yúshì wǒmen juédìng huí jiā.
example.english: It started raining, so we decided to go home.
example.fact: 于是 links two clauses in a strict cause-then-effect sequence and always follows the cause — unlike 因为...所以... it can't front the reason first — making it closer to English "and so" or "thereupon," narrating what happened next rather than formally explaining why.

examples.pinyin: Tā lèi le, yúshì zǎozǎo shuì le.
examples.english: He was tired, so he went to bed early.

examples.hanzi: 我们看到朋友在招手，于是走了过去。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen kàndào péngyou zài zhāoshǒu, yúshì zǒule guòqù.
examples.english: We saw our friend waving, so we walked over.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
戈 (halberd) — a weapon radical, as in 战 war and 成. 我 began as a picture of a jagged-bladed weapon; the pronoun "I" is a later borrowing of the sound.

example.hanzi: 每个人都应该学会自我反省。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yīnggāi xuéhuì zìwǒ fǎnxǐng.
example.english: Everyone should learn to reflect on themselves.
example.fact: 自我 almost always attaches as a prefix before another verb or noun — 自我反省 ("self-reflection"), 自我介绍 ("self-introduction"), 自我保护 ("self-protection") — rather than standing alone the way English "self" can; for a stand-alone reflexive pronoun, Chinese instead reaches for 自己.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ xiān zuò ge zìwǒ jièshào.
examples.english: Please give a self-introduction first.

examples.pinyin: Yào yǒu zìwǒ bǎohù de yìshí.
examples.english: You should have a sense of self-protection.

meanings: (dialect) (usu. used in the negative) to get along with (sb)

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 付 is handing 寸 something to a person.
付 (fù) is also the sound in 附 fù, 府 fǔ, 符 fú and 腐 fǔ.

example.hanzi: 这种情况我们该怎么对付?
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng qíngkuàng wǒmen gāi zěnme duìfu?
example.english: How should we deal with this kind of situation?
example.fact: 对付 usually carries a faint sense of makeshift or reluctant effort — "handling" something you'd rather not have to — which is why it also extends to 对付一下 ("make do for now") in a way that the more neutral, businesslike 处理 ("to handle, process") does not.

examples.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, wǒ huì duìfu tā de.
examples.english: Don't worry, I'll deal with him.

examples.pinyin: Zhè diǎn qián zhǐ néng duìfu jǐ tiān.
examples.english: This little money can only get us by for a few days.

components.note: 非 (not) — two wings spread in opposite directions, so "opposed, not". Gives sound to 啡 fēi, 排 pái and 悲 bēi.

example.hanzi: 我非去不可。
example.pinyin: Wǒ fēi qù bùkě.
example.english: I absolutely have to go.
example.fact: 非 is a formal "not" and a prefix "non-": 非法 (illegal). 非 … 不可 means "must" (literally "not doing X is not acceptable"). 非常 ("very") is literally "not ordinary", and 非洲 is Africa.

examples.pinyin: Tā fēicháng nǔlì.
examples.english: He is extremely hardworking.

examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò shì fēifǎ de.
examples.english: Doing this is illegal.

meanings: good action, deed, thing or work
Daoist or Buddhist ceremony for the souls of the dead

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 帮助别人是一件好事。
example.pinyin: Bāngzhù biérén shì yí jiàn hǎoshì.
example.english: Helping others is a good thing.
example.fact: 好事 is a case where tone alone splits two unrelated words: read hǎoshì (as here) it means "a good deed"; read hàoshì — identical characters, different tones — it instead becomes an adjective for someone "meddlesome, eager to stir up trouble." Context and tone, not spelling, are all that separate a compliment from a complaint.

examples.pinyin: Tā zuòle hěn duō hǎoshì.
examples.english: He has done many good deeds.

examples.pinyin: Yǒu hǎoshì jiù gàosu wǒ yì shēng.
examples.english: If there's good news, let me know.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and prayer: 神, 福, 祝; 祈 is to pray.
斤 (jīn) is only a loose sound clue for qí.
礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and prayer: 神, 福, 祈; 祷 is to pray aloud.
寿 (shòu) is only a loose sound clue; same part in 涛 tāo.

example.hanzi: 她闭上眼睛,轻声祈祷。
example.pinyin: Tā bìshàng yǎnjīng, qīngshēng qídǎo.
example.english: She closed her eyes and prayed quietly.
example.fact: Both halves of 祈祷 carry the 礻 radical — a simplified altar/spirit-tablet shape also seen in 神 ("god") and 祝 ("to wish, bless") — marking the word as belonging to a whole family of characters tied to ritual and worship.

examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu zài wèi tā qídǎo.
examples.english: Everyone is praying for him.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān wǎnshang dōu huì qídǎo.
examples.english: I pray every night.

components.note: 元 (first, head) — a person with the head marked: 元 first meant the head, so first, chief, origin. 元 also gives 完 wán, 玩 wán and 院 yuàn.

example.hanzi: 这本书二十元。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū èrshí yuán.
example.english: This book costs twenty yuan.
example.fact: 元 is the formal word for the yuan, found on banknotes, while speech uses 块 (kuài): 二十块. It also means first or origin: 元旦 (New Year's Day), 元首 (head of state), and 元宵 is the Lantern Festival.

examples.pinyin: Zhège bēizi zhǐyào wǔshí yuán.
examples.english: This cup only costs fifty yuan.

examples.pinyin: Yīyuè yī rì shì Yuándàn.
examples.english: January 1st is New Year's Day.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and weaving, as in 线, 红, 绳; 编 is to weave, then to compile.
扁 (biǎn) gives the sound: 编 biān is close, as in 偏 piān and 篇 piān.

example.hanzi: 她会编织毛衣。
example.pinyin: Tā huì biānzhī máoyī.
example.english: She knows how to knit sweaters.
example.fact: 编 is to weave or braid (编辫子), and by extension to compile or compose: 编辑 (editor), 编程 (to program), 编号 (serial number). 编故事 can mean to invent a story, and 你别瞎编 means "stop making things up".

examples.hanzi: 他在编一个很有趣的故事。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài biān yí gè hěn yǒuqù de gùshi.
examples.english: He is making up a very interesting story.

examples.pinyin: Zhè běn cídiǎn shì tāmen biān de.
examples.english: This dictionary was compiled by them.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 拾 is to pick up. It is also a formal way to write ten.
合 (hé) is a loose sound hint.

example.hanzi: 出门前,请把房间收拾好。
example.pinyin: Chūmén qián, qǐng bǎ fángjiān shōushi hǎo.
example.english: Before going out, please tidy up the room.
example.fact: 收拾 can shift from its literal "tidy up, pack" sense into a colloquial threat — 我要收拾你了 means "I'm going to sort you out" — using the verb the same way English "sort out" can describe either organizing a room or handling a person roughly.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shōushi yíxià xíngli ba.
examples.english: Pack your luggage, please.

examples.hanzi: 他把东西收拾好就出门了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ dōngxi shōushi hǎo jiù chūmén le.
examples.english: He tidied up his things and went out.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; a guest is a person under your roof.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 路 lù, 洛 luò, 落 luò.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 今晚家里有客人,我们得准备晚饭。
example.pinyin: Jīnwǎn jiālǐ yǒu kèrén, wǒmen děi zhǔnbèi wǎnfàn.
example.english: We have guests at home tonight, so we need to prepare dinner.
example.fact: 客人 pairs 客 ("guest," built from a roof 宀 sheltering an arriving visitor 各) with the generic suffix 人 ("person") — the same 客 root gives 顾客 ("customer," a guest who pays) and 乘客 ("passenger," a guest riding along), all sharing the core image of someone welcomed in from outside.

examples.pinyin: Huānyíng kèren jìn wū zuò.
examples.english: Welcome the guests to come in and sit.

examples.pinyin: Fàndiàn lǐ kèren hěn duō.
examples.english: The restaurant has a lot of guests.

components.note: 犬 (dog) — animals: 狗, 猫; 状 first meant the shape of an animal.
丬 (a form of 爿) gives zhuàng: also in 壮 zhuàng, 装 zhuāng, 将 jiāng and 奖 jiǎng.
心 (heart) — feelings and attitudes: 想, 思, 感; 态 is one's attitude.
太 (tài) sounds exactly like 态.

example.hanzi: 他最近的身体状态不太好。
example.pinyin: Tā zuìjìn de shēntǐ zhuàngtài bú tài hǎo.
example.english: His physical condition hasn't been very good lately.
example.fact: 状态 is also the standard word for "state" in science class — 固态/液态/气态 (solid/liquid/gaseous state) all reuse the 态 root — and in sports and gaming slang, 状态好/状态不好 ("in good/bad form") has become a casual, everyday way to talk about how someone is performing on a given day.

examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān de zhuàngtài hěn hǎo.
examples.english: She is in great form today.

examples.hanzi: 我想知道这个软件的状态。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zhīdào zhè ge ruǎnjiàn de zhuàngtài.
examples.english: I want to know the status of this software.

components.note: 戈 (halberd, weapon) — war and weapons: 我, 成, 武, 伐; here fighting.
占 (zhàn) sounds exactly like 战; also in 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 两国之间发生了战争。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó zhījiān fāshēng le zhànzhēng.
example.english: A war broke out between the two countries.
example.fact: 战 is bound to compounds: 战争 (war), 战斗 (fight), 战士 (soldier), 挑战 (challenge), 战胜 (defeat), 冷战 (Cold War). It also works in sports and games as "match", as in 战队.

examples.hanzi: 战争给人们带来了很多痛苦。
examples.pinyin: Zhànzhēng gěi rénmen dàilái le hěn duō tòngkǔ.
examples.english: War brought great suffering to people.

examples.hanzi: 这场比赛我们一定要战胜对手。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng bǐsài wǒmen yídìng yào zhànshèng duìshǒu.
examples.english: We must defeat our opponent in this match.

components.note: 亚 (yà) — Asia; as a part it sounds out 哑 yǎ and 娅 yà.

example.hanzi: 中国在亚洲。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó zài Yàzhōu.
example.english: China is in Asia.
example.fact: 亚 is short for 亚洲 (Asia), taken from the sound of "Asia". It also means "second" or "sub-": 亚军 (runner-up) and 亚热带 (subtropics). It appears in transliterations, such as 亚马逊 (Amazon).

examples.hanzi: 我爸爸去过很多亚洲国家。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba qù guo hěn duō Yàzhōu guójiā.
examples.english: My dad has been to many Asian countries.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng dé le yàjūn.
examples.english: He won second place in the competition.

components.note: 周 (zhōu) also lends its sound to 调 diào/tiáo, 稠 chóu, 绸 chóu and 凋 diāo.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国, 园, 图; 围 is to surround.
韦 (wéi) sounds exactly like 围; also in 违 wéi and 伟 wěi.

example.hanzi: 公园周围有很多商店。
example.pinyin: Gōngyuán zhōuwéi yǒu hěn duō shāngdiàn.
example.english: There are many shops around the park.
example.fact: 周围 combines two characters that both independently suggest enclosure — 周 (an old word for a bounded territory) and 围 ("to surround," built from the enclosure radical 囗) — reinforcing each other into a word that always describes the space encircling something, never a single point.

examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào zhōuwéi hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: It's very quiet around the school.

examples.hanzi: 他看了看周围，一个人也没有。
examples.pinyin: Tā kànle kàn zhōuwéi, yí ge rén yě méiyǒu.
examples.english: He looked around and nobody was there.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.hanzi: 这家电视台对这次事件做了详细的报道。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diànshìtái duì zhè cì shìjiàn zuò le xiángxì de bàodào.
example.english: This TV station did a detailed report on the incident.
example.fact: 报道 is the standard word for journalistic reporting, distinct from the similar-looking 报告 (bàogào, "a report" in the sense of a formal written document, like a school or business report) — despite differing by only one character, the two words are not interchangeable.

examples.hanzi: 报纸上报道了这个好消息。
examples.pinyin: Bàozhǐ shàng bàodàole zhè ge hǎo xiāoxi.
examples.english: The newspaper reported this good news.

examples.pinyin: Zhè piān bàodào xiě de hěn xiángxì.
examples.english: This report is written in great detail.

components.note: 戈 (halberd) — weapons, as in 战 war and 成; the traditional 戲 was a play or contest.

example.hanzi: 这场戏很精彩。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng xì hěn jīngcǎi.
example.english: This play is very exciting.
example.fact: 戏 is a play or a performance, counted with 场. 看戏 means to watch a play, and 戏剧 is drama. 游戏 is a game, and 戏精 is internet slang for an overly dramatic person.

examples.hanzi: 我们周末去看了一场京戏。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù kàn le yì chǎng jīngxì.
examples.english: We went to see a Peking opera at the weekend.

examples.pinyin: Zhè háizi hěn ài yǎnxì.
examples.english: This child loves acting.

components.note: 参 (cān) is a sound clue for 惨 cǎn and 掺 chān; the old shape pictured three stars.
The shape does not explain 与 today (simplified from 與, two hands handing something over). Memory aid: a hand passing a thing along, hence 'give' and then 'and, with'.

example.hanzi: 很多学生都参与了这次活动。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō xuésheng dōu cānyù le zhè cì huódòng.
example.english: Many students participated in this event.
example.fact: 参与 is a shade more formal than the everyday 参加 ("to take part in, attend") — 参与 often stresses being involved in a process or decision (参与决策, "to participate in decision-making"), while 参加 more simply names attending an event (参加聚会, "attend a party"), a nuance easy for learners to blur.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng cānyù zhè ge xiàngmù ma?
examples.english: Would you like to take part in this project?

examples.hanzi: 每个人都应该参与讨论。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge rén dōu yīnggāi cānyù tǎolùn.
examples.english: Everyone should take part in the discussion.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 运 is to move, then to be moved by luck.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for yùn.
力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.

example.hanzi: 医生建议他每天运动半小时。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì tā měitiān yùndòng bàn xiǎoshí.
example.english: The doctor recommended he exercise for half an hour every day.
example.fact: 运动 stretches across three registers at once — physics' "motion" (物体的运动), everyday "exercise" (as here), and history's capital-M "Movement" (五四运动, the May Fourth Movement) — all sharing the same underlying idea of something set in motion, whether a body, a muscle, or a whole society.

examples.hanzi: 我早上喜欢运动一会儿。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǎoshang xǐhuan yùndòng yíhuìr.
examples.english: I like exercising for a while in the morning.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan shénme yùndòng?
examples.english: What sports do you like?

components.note: 彳 (step, left foot) — walking and roads: 行, 往, 很, 得, 德; 彼 points out that, the other.
皮 (pí) is a loose sound clue; same part in 披 pī, 被 bèi, 破 pò.
此 (cǐ) is a sound clue for 紫 zǐ, 雌 cí and 些 xiē; as a word it means "this".

example.hanzi: 我们应该彼此信任。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi bǐcǐ xìnrèn.
example.english: We should trust each other.
example.fact: 彼此 fuses two demonstrative roots meaning "that" (彼) and "this" (此) into a single reciprocal pronoun — a compositional logic close to English's own "each other," which likewise builds a mutual idea by pairing two separate pointing words.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen bǐcǐ dōu hěn liǎojiě.
examples.english: They know each other very well.

examples.hanzi: 我们彼此彼此，都不容易。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bǐcǐ bǐcǐ, dōu bù róngyì.
examples.english: The same to you, neither of us has it easy.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — flowers and growth: 花, 草, 茶; 荣 (from 榮) is a tree 木 in full bloom: flourishing, honor.
幸 (luck) — often read as an old picture of shackles; 'luck' is escaping punishment. The dictionary story (one alive 土, one dead 干) is a memory aid.
土 (earth) — the top. Memory aid: the one standing on solid ground 土 is the lucky one — 幸运, 幸福.

example.hanzi: 能认识您,我感到很荣幸。
example.pinyin: Néng rènshi nín, wǒ gǎndào hěn róngxìng.
example.english: I feel very honored to meet you.
example.fact: 荣幸 sits at the formal, politeness-register end of Chinese — common in introductions and speeches (很荣幸认识您, "it's an honor to meet you") but rarely reached for over small, everyday favors, where English "honored" can sometimes sound sarcastic if overused casually; 荣幸 keeps a consistently sincere, formal tone instead.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de róngxìng.
examples.english: It's my honor.

examples.hanzi: 我很荣幸能参加你们的婚礼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn róngxìng néng cānjiā nǐmen de hūnlǐ.
examples.english: I'm honored to attend your wedding.

components.note: 会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 话 speech; 议 is to discuss.
义 (yì) sounds exactly like 议; same part in 仪 yí and 蚁 yǐ.

example.hanzi: 明天上午九点有一个重要的会议。
example.pinyin: Míngtiān shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn yǒu yí gè zhòngyào de huìyì.
example.english: There's an important meeting tomorrow at nine in the morning.
example.fact: 会议 is the formal, official word for a scheduled meeting, the kind on a corporate calendar, while a casual get-together among friends is called 聚会 instead — both share the root 会 ("to meet, gather"), but their second halves signal a difference in register a bare dictionary entry doesn't always convey.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiàwǔ liǎng diǎn kāi huìyì.
examples.english: We have a meeting at two in the afternoon.

examples.hanzi: 这次国际会议有一百个国家参加。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì guójì huìyì yǒu yì bǎi ge guójiā cānjiā.
examples.english: A hundred countries are taking part in this international conference.

components.note: 至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 达 is to get through to, to reach.
大 (dà) is only a loose stand-in for the old sound part, so treat it as a rough clue for dá.

example.hanzi: 火车将于晚上八点到达北京。
example.pinyin: Huǒchē jiāng yú wǎnshàng bā diǎn dàodá Běijīng.
example.english: The train will arrive in Beijing at eight in the evening.
example.fact: 到达 is the formal, written-register match for the everyday spoken verb 到 — a train schedule or news report says 到达, but a friend texting you would more naturally just write 我到了 ("I've arrived") rather than the stiffer-sounding 我到达了.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jǐ diǎn néng dàodá jīchǎng?
examples.english: What time can you reach the airport?

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōngyú dàodále shāndǐng.
examples.english: We finally reached the mountaintop.

components.note: 爪 (claw, hand) — marks grasping hands and claws, as in 抓 grab; 爬 is crawling and climbing using the hands.
巴 (bā) — loose sound hint (pá vs bā); 巴 also sounds out 吧 ba and 把 bǎ.

example.hanzi: 小孩子在地板上爬。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi zài dìbǎn shang pá.
example.english: The little child is crawling on the floor.
example.fact: 爬 is to crawl or climb, as in 爬山 (hike), 爬楼梯 (climb the stairs). In tech it appears in 网络爬虫 (web crawler), literally "crawling bug". 登 (dēng) is the more formal "climb".

examples.pinyin: Tā páshàngle nà zuò shān.
examples.english: He climbed up that mountain.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎomāo pá dào le shù shang.
examples.english: The kitten climbed up the tree.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is the money radical — 财, 贵, 买, 费; betting stakes money.
者 (zhě) — near hint — 赌 is dǔ; 者 also sounds out 堵 dǔ and 都 dū.

example.hanzi: 我不喜欢赌钱。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bù xǐhuan dǔ qián.
example.english: I don't like gambling.
example.fact: 赌 is to gamble or bet: 赌钱, 赌博 (gambling, formal), 赌场 (casino), 打赌 (to make a bet). 赌气 ("gamble breath") is a different idea: to act out of spite or sulk.

examples.hanzi: 他输了很多钱，因为他爱赌。
examples.pinyin: Tā shū le hěn duō qián, yīnwèi tā ài dǔ.
examples.english: He lost a lot of money because he loves gambling.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gǎn hé nǐ dǔ yì bēi kāfēi.
examples.english: I'll bet you a cup of coffee.

components.note: 日 (sun) — light and brightness: 明, 晴, 时; 显 is something lit up and clear to see.
示 (show) — an altar, a table for offerings; as the radical 礻 it marks rites and spirits: 神, 礼, 福, 社, 祝.

example.hanzi: 数据显示,今年的销量比去年高。
example.pinyin: Shùjù xiǎnshì, jīnnián de xiāoliàng bǐ qùnián gāo.
example.english: The data shows that this year's sales are higher than last year's.
example.fact: 显示 is also the standard word for a computer or phone display — 显示器 is "monitor" and 显示屏 is "display screen" — extending its written-register sense of "to reveal, indicate" into the literal hardware that shows images on a screen.

examples.hanzi: 屏幕上显示今天的天气。
examples.pinyin: Píngmù shàng xiǎnshì jīntiān de tiānqì.
examples.english: The screen shows today's weather.

examples.hanzi: 这个结果显示他很努力。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jiéguǒ xiǎnshì tā hěn nǔlì.
examples.english: This result shows that he worked hard.

components.note: 阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 队 is a group of people gathered together.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 伍 is a squad of five people.
五 (wǔ) sounds exactly like 伍 — and means five; also in 吾 wú and 悟 wù.

example.hanzi: 一大早,门口就排起了长长的队伍。
example.pinyin: Yí dà zǎo, ménkǒu jiù pái qǐ le chángcháng de duìwu.
example.english: Early in the morning, a long line had already formed at the entrance.
example.fact: 队伍 originally described soldiers marching in formation, but modern usage has broadened it into the everyday word for any line of people waiting — 排队伍, alongside the more common 排队 ("to queue"), still draws on the same military image of people falling into an orderly row.

examples.hanzi: 我们的队伍有二十个人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de duìwu yǒu èrshí ge rén.
examples.english: Our team has twenty people.

examples.hanzi: 游行的队伍走过了街道。
examples.pinyin: Yóuxíng de duìwu zǒuguòle jiēdào.
examples.english: The parade passed through the streets.

components.note: 立 (stand) — a person standing on the ground line. As a radical it appears in 站 stand, 位 seat, 竟; also in 建立 establish.
刂 (knife) — cutting and sharpness: 利, 别, 到; 刻 is to carve, and the carved marks on a clock became quarter hours.
亥 (hài) is only a loose sound hint; same part in 孩 hái and 核 hé.

example.hanzi: 听到消息后,他立刻打电话给妈妈。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào xiāoxi hòu, tā lìkè dǎ diànhuà gěi māma.
example.english: After hearing the news, he immediately called his mom.
example.fact: 立刻 sits among a cluster of near-synonymous "immediately" adverbs — 马上, 立刻, and 立即 — that are largely interchangeable in casual speech, with 立即 leaning slightly more formal and written, a register distinction dictionaries rarely spell out for near-synonyms.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ lìkè huí jiā ba.
examples.english: Go home right now.

examples.hanzi: 他一说完就立刻离开了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì shuōwán jiù lìkè líkāi le.
examples.english: He left immediately after he finished speaking.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 给, 经: cutting a thread, hence to break off.
色 (sè) is only a loose sound clue for jué.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.

example.hanzi: 我绝不会放弃我的梦想。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jué bú huì fàngqì wǒ de mèngxiǎng.
example.english: I will never give up on my dream.
example.fact: 绝 already means "to cut off completely" on its own (绝望 "to give up hope," 绝交 "to break off a friendship") — prefixed onto 不, it turns a plain negative into an emphatic one, working like English "absolutely not" rather than a soft "not really."

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jué bù xiāngxìn tā.
examples.english: I absolutely don't believe him.

examples.pinyin: Tā jué bú huì chídào de.
examples.english: He will definitely not be late.

components.note: 舛 (two opposed feet) — the dancer's footwork; 無 (wú) above is a loose sound clue, as it once meant dance itself.
台 (tái) as a sound part appears in 抬 tái, 胎 tāi, 苔 tái, and also in 治 zhì and 始 shǐ.

example.hanzi: 她第一次站在舞台上唱歌,非常紧张。
example.pinyin: Tā dì-yī cì zhàn zài wǔtái shàng chàng gē, fēicháng jǐnzhāng.
example.english: The first time she stood on stage to sing, she was extremely nervous.
example.fact: 舞台 literally means "dance platform" (舞 "to dance" + 台 "platform, stage") — even though modern stages host far more than dance, from theater to political speeches (政治舞台, "the political stage/arena"), the word still carries its original image of a raised performance space.

examples.pinyin: Wǔtái shàng de dēngguāng hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: The lights on the stage are beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 这个舞台是为明星准备的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge wǔtái shì wèi míngxīng zhǔnbèi de.
examples.english: This stage was prepared for celebrities.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — spitting out; also in 叫 shout, 吃 eat.
土 (tǔ) gives the exact sound (tǔ), also read tù as in 呕吐.

example.hanzi: 别在地上吐痰。
example.pinyin: Bié zài dì shang tǔ tán.
example.english: Don't spit on the ground.
example.fact: 吐 is read tǔ for spitting or letting something out (吐出来), and tù for vomiting (呕吐, 吐了). The internet word 吐槽 (tǔcáo) means to roast or complain humorously about something.

examples.hanzi: 他吐了一口气，终于放心了。
examples.pinyin: Tā tǔ le yì kǒu qì, zhōngyú fàngxīn le.
examples.english: He let out a breath and finally felt relieved.

examples.hanzi: 吃坏了东西，他吐了一晚上。
examples.pinyin: Chī huài le dōngxi, tā tù le yì wǎnshang.
examples.english: He ate something bad and threw up all night.
